prior_nu4_diagnostic.relation: The 49/49 nu=4 observation is subsumed by the theorem proved here.

frozen_structure.admissible_channel_family: Every admissible X is an arbitrary subgraph of K_{2,2}[A,E] disjoint_union K_{2,2}[B,D].

theorem.statement: For every admissible descendant C_X of the frozen frame, kappa(C_X)=lambda_{C_X}(c0,f0)=1+nu(X).

upper_bound.construction: Let U be a minimum vertex cover of the bipartite channel graph X. Remove {z} union U.
reason: Removing z destroys the unique hub channel between the two octahedral sides.
U meets every direct cross-block edge in X.
The frozen frame contains no other inter-block edges.
The anchors c0 and f0 are not in {z} union U, so they lie in distinct surviving components.
upper_bound.conclusion: The same explicit cut gives both lambda_CX(c0,f0)<=1+nu(X) and global kappa(C_X)<=1+nu(X).

lower_bound_nu_le_3.claim: For nu(X)<=3, deleting any S with |S|<=nu(X) leaves C_X connected.

proof_cases.argument: Each octahedron loses at most three vertices and remains connected because K_{2,2,2} is 4-connected. Each side has four frozen neighbors of z, so at most three deletions cannot remove all z-neighbors on either side. Thus z connects the two surviving connected octahedral sides.

At most nu(X)-1 vertices remain available outside z. A vertex set of size at most nu(X)-1 cannot cover all channel edges because tau(X)=nu(X). Hence some cross-edge uv survives. Each octahedron has lost at most two vertices when nu<=3 and is connected, so the surviving edge uv joins the two connected sides.

lower_bound_nu_eq_4.premise: nu(X)=4, so X contains a perfect matching covering all four left ports A union B and all four right ports D union E.
lower_bound_nu_eq_4.claim: Deleting any S with |S|<=4 leaves C_X connected.

proof_cases.argument: The previous z/not-z argument applies verbatim: with z present neither side can lose all four z-neighbors; with z deleted fewer than four remaining deletions cannot cover all channel edges.

Only three other deletions remain. Since tau(X)=4, at least one cross-edge survives. Each octahedron loses at most three vertices and remains connected, so the surviving cross-edge joins the two sides.

proof_cases.case: |S|=4, z not in S, and each octahedron loses at most three vertices
proof_cases.argument: Both octahedra remain connected and each retains at least one of its four z-neighbors, hence z joins them.

proof_cases.case: |S|=4, z not in S, and all four deletions lie in one octahedron
proof_cases.argument: The opposite octahedron is intact. On the damaged left side, every surviving vertex in A union C is adjacent to z, while every surviving B-port has its distinct matched D-neighbor intact on the right. The symmetric statement holds when the right side is damaged: every surviving D union F vertex is adjacent to z, while every surviving E-port has its matched A-neighbor intact on the left. Therefore every surviving vertex belongs to the same component.

theorem.equality: Combining the global upper cut with the lower bound gives kappa(C_X)=1+nu(X). Binding with the previously sealed exact anchor theorem gives kappa(C_X)=lambda_CX(c0,f0)=1+nu(X).

canonical_nu4_cuts.explanation: For nu(X)=4, X has perfect matching number four and the frozen support is K_{2,2}[A,E] disjoint_union K_{2,2}[B,D]. The four sets A union B, A union D, B union E, D union E are size-4 vertex covers of every support subgraph and therefore minimum covers for every nu=4 descendant.
